findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is divisible by limit
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For a group with exactly 100 members and limit 50, this yields 3 pages when only 2 exist. Since showingLast compares currentPage to totalPages, the user can click "next" past the real last page; the next action sets offset to min(offset + limit, user_count) (i.e. 100), and findMembers then fetches an empty page, showing a blank member list on page "3/3". The computation should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group test uses PUT instead of DELETE
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route added in config/routes.rb maps remove_member to DELETE members (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT members is mapped to add_members. This request therefore routes to add_members, which requires a :usernames param and will raise rather than return 422, so the test does not exercise the code path it claims to and will fail (or pass for the wrong reason) once run against the real routes.

findings.title: add_members does not strip whitespace around usernames
findings.body: add_members splits the usernames param on "," and passes each fragment directly to User.find_by_username without stripping whitespace. A common input like "alice, bob" (with a space after the comma) makes the lookup for " bob" fail silently, so bob is not added and the admin gets no error — the success response hides the skipped user. Each fragment should be stripped before lookup, and ideally unknown usernames should be reported back instead of being silently ignored.
